# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Security Health Plan — Member Appeals
*(Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.)*

**From:** Quinn Delgado
**Member ID:** W149862261
**Reference number:** POC-5142E8878F-52764
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-07

**RE: Appeal of the denial of prior authorization for shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806 — reviewed under *eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures* (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf)**

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing Security Health Plan's decision, dated 2026-08-07, to deny prior authorization for the shoulder labral / instability repair (CPT 29806) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that determination, because the records already in my file line up with the criteria published in the guideline named above.

I am not a doctor, and I am not asking the plan to take my word for my condition. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the clinical records submitted with the prior authorization request support that. Below, I have set the plan's own published criteria next to what those records say.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging showing labral/capsular pathology that correlates with symptoms and exam.** The guideline states:

> "MRI or CT shows labral/capsular pathology (e.g., Bankart, capsular tear) and correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings"

My MR arthrogram of the shoulder, performed 2026-06-25, shows an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff. This is the exact lesion the guideline names. It matches what I feel — nine months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension — and it matches what my surgeon found on examination.

**2. Positive orthopedic tests on exam.** The guideline states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates ANY of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs (as compared to the non-involved side):"

and among the listed signs:

> "Anterior or posterior apprehension test"

My exam documents positive apprehension and relocation tests, increased anterior translation on load-and-shift, and full strength. The apprehension test the guideline names is positive in my case.

**3. Documented instability causing function-limiting pain.** The guideline states:

> "Documented histo ry of " post-traumatic" or " atraumatic" instability and/or laxity that has resul ted in function-limiting pain"

and refers to:

> "with the abi lity to carry out ag e appropriate activities of daily living a nd/or demands of employment)"

I have had three anterior dislocations since my symptoms began, the most recent one reduced in the emergency department. I avoid overhead reaching, and I cannot return to my work lifting. My shoulder instability is limiting both my daily activities and my job.

**4. Other conditions considered.** The guideline states:

> "Other potential pathological cond itions have been excluded including, but not limited to, the following: fracture, thoracic outlet syndrome, b rachial ple xus disorders, referred neck pain, cervical radiculopathy, a nd advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis"

My imaging and examination point to one source: anterior glenohumeral instability from an anteroinferior labral (Bankart) tear, with the rotator cuff intact. No other diagnosis appears in my records as the cause of my symptoms. If the reviewer believes a specific alternative condition on this list was not adequately addressed, I ask that it be identified by name so my surgeon can respond to it directly.

## The conservative care requirement

I want to address this criterion plainly rather than talk around it. The guideline states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration that includes shoulder stabilization/strengthening exercises"

My documented course of supervised physical therapy — focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification — ran from 2026-04-05 to 2026-06-14, which is 10 weeks, with 24 visits completed, as recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. That is the precise type of provider-directed stabilization and strengthening program the guideline describes, and it was pursued intensively. I also took NSAIDs for four months during flares; no injection was given, as it is not indicated for instability.

During and after that program, my shoulder continued to dislocate, and my symptoms have now run nine months. My records also note the guideline's own exception language:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required in an acute traumatic injury setting when EITHER of the following conditions are present:"

The excerpt of the guideline available to me ends at that colon and lists conditions I have not been given in full; one of them reads:

> "A nterior shoulder instability in competitive contact or collision athletes"

I am not claiming any condition that is not in my records, and I am not asking the plan to assume I meet an exception it has not shown me. I am asking that the exception list be provided in writing so that my surgeon and I can address whether any part of it applies to my situation.

Finally, the guideline itself states:

> "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of shoulder surgery is always made on a case-by-case basis."

On the facts of my case — three documented anterior dislocations including one requiring emergency department reduction, a Bankart lesion with a small Hill-Sachs lesion on MR arthrogram, positive apprehension and relocation testing, and 24 completed physical therapy visits that did not stop the dislocations — I am asking for that individual review.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

The denial notice states that the decision was made under "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," but it does not tell me which criteria those were or how my records fell short of them. The plan holds those criteria, and I am requesting them in writing:

- the complete guideline and criteria set actually applied to CPT 29806 in my case, including the full list of positive orthopedic tests and the full list of criteria-exception conditions that follow the colons in the excerpts above;
- the identity of any reviewing entity, including eviCore, whose guidelines were used;
- any internal Security Health Plan medical policy relied on, including any policy hosted on the plan's PolicyTech site or any policy that is no longer publicly reachable because it redirects to a login page; and
- the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination.

I am asking for these as part of this appeal so that I can respond specifically to whatever standard was used.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Security Health Plan overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 (reference POC-5142E8878F-52764) and authorize the shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion my records failed to meet and the specific evidence the reviewer found lacking, along with information about my right to an independent external review.

Per the denial notice, this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-03**. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not correct for member appeals, I ask that the plan route this letter to the correct department and notify me.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. My surgeon's office has indicated it will provide whatever documentation the plan requests.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Delgado**
Member ID: W149862261
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-07 (reference POC-5142E8878F-52764)
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-06-25
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-05 to 2026-06-14, 24 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Emergency department record for shoulder dislocation reduction
- [Any other records you wish to attach]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
